slide1.text: Harvey Washington Wiley was an American physician and chemist. He was the [[first commissioner of the United States Food and Drug Administration]].

slide2.heading: Government career
paras: Wiley was appropriated $5,000 in 1902 to study the effects of a diet including various preservatives, on human volunteers. The subjects received $5 a month and free food to be systematically poisoned. First to be tested was borax which tightened old meat which was starting to decompose. These "[[poison squad]]" studies drew national attention to the need for a federal food and drug law.

slide3.heading: Work at Good Housekeeping
paras: In a famous action he brought against The Coca-Cola Company in 1911, he contended that it was illegal to use the name Coca-Cola when there was no actual cocaine in the drink, and also that it was illegal for it to contain caffeine as an additive. Perversely, this was as much as to say that the product [[ought to have contained cocaine and not caffeine]].

Harvey Washington Wiley.caption: Harvey Washington Wiley: before he became the first head of the FDA, he paid volunteers $5 a month to eat meals laced with preservatives like borax, a group that became known as the "Poison Squad."

slide1.text: Lowercase is an extreme form of ambient minimalism in which [[very quiet sounds are amplified to extreme levels]].

slide2.heading: Origins
paras: Minimal artist Steve Roden popularized the movement with an album entitled Forms of Paper, in which he made [[recordings of himself handling paper]] in various ways. These recordings were commissioned by the Hollywood branch of the Los Angeles Public Library.

slide3.heading: Definition
paras: Steve Roden stated this about the lowercase tendencies which he began to develop in his later works: “It bears a certain sense of quiet and humility; it doesn't demand attention, it must be discovered. [[It’s the opposite of capital letters]]—loud things which draw attention to themselves.”

Lowercase (music).caption: Lowercase (music): a genre built on tiny, quiet sounds turned up very loud. It took off with an album of an artist recording himself handling paper.

slide1.text: This is a list of people notable for [[living for periods of more than a week in airports]]. The reasons are usually protesting, asylum seeking or having difficulty with visas and passports.

extraSlides.heading: Edward Snowden
paras: While on a flight to Moscow-Sheremetyevo, authorities [[revoked Snowden's U.S. passport]].
He was granted temporary asylum in Russia. He later received Russian citizenship.

extraSlides.heading: Mehran Karimi Nasseri
paras: Originally from Iran, Nasseri was given refugee status by UNHCR and claimed that [[his documents were stolen]] in Paris en route to the United Kingdom.
He was refused entry and declined new papers due to [[changing his own name and place of birth]].

extraSlides.heading: Wei Jianguo
paras: Wei wanted to [[smoke and drink without his family bothering him]]. He also had difficulty finding work.
He still lives in the airport, but comes out occasionally.

image.file: File:Beijing Capital International Airport Terminal 3 Interior 20090818.jpg

extraSlides.heading: Hiroshi Nohara
paras: Nohara [[declined to give his reasons]].
He left with [[a woman identified as Oyuki]].

extraSlides.heading: Heinz Müller
paras: Müller flew to Rio de Janeiro to meet with [[a woman he met online, who did not show up]]. He ran out of money and ended up in Campinas.

extraSlides.heading: Bayram Tepeli
paras: Tepeli ran away from family problems and worked at the airport for a while. Eventually he became sick, and could not work anymore, but [[decided to keep living at the airport]].
The airport closed for commercial passenger travel in 2019, so he had to leave. He now lives in Sabiha Gökçen Airport.

extraSlides.heading: Aditya Singh
paras: Singh [[decided not to take his connecting flight]] to India due to fear of COVID-19.
He was arrested in January 2021, but cleared of charges in late 2021.

extraSlides.heading: Sanjay Shah
paras: Shah spent 13 months [[living in the duty-free section]] of Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, petitioning for full British citizenship. This was eventually granted on the grounds that he had already given up his former Kenyan citizenship.

List of people who have lived in airport.caption: List of people who have lived in airports: one man lived in Paris's Charles de Gaulle Airport for nearly 18 years, and another moved into Beijing's airport so he could smoke and drink without his family bothering him.

slide1.text: Romeo and Juliet are a pair of [[female mute swans]] that previously resided in the pond of the Public Garden of Boston, Massachusetts, United States, during the spring and summer months.

slide2.heading: A surprise
paras: The same two swans were introduced yearly to the Public Garden since 2003, but were not discovered to both be female until 2005. The swans were obtained from a breeder who had informed the city's Parks and Recreation Department that both were female. Park rangers had assumed that the breeder [[mistakenly provided a male swan]] when the pair began exhibiting parenting behavior.

slide3.heading: Return of the Swans
paras: The swans resided at the Franklin Park Zoo during the winter months and were reintroduced to the Public Garden during the annual Return of the Swans celebration. The swans are escorted to the garden's pond by a [[parade and brass band]] and then released into the water during the ceremony.

Romeo and Juliet (swans).caption: Romeo and Juliet (swans): Boston's famous swan couple turned out to both be female, even though the breeder had said so all along. Each spring the city escorted them back to their pond with a parade and a brass band.

image.file: File:Boston Public Garden Swan Nesting Area (cropped).jpg

slide1.text: The community was known as Mole Hill prior to 1949, when residents requested that the name be changed to Mountain as part of a publicity stunt to [[literally make a mountain out of a molehill]].

slide2.heading: Despite the name
paras: Mountain is an unincorporated community in Ritchie County, West Virginia, United States. Despite the name, there is [[no mountain in or even visible from the community]].

slide3.heading: Mole Hill
paras: The community most likely was named after the [[local Mole family]].
The post office ultimately closed on November 9, 2002.

Mountain, West Virginia.caption: Mountain, West Virginia: this tiny community used to be called Mole Hill, until residents renamed it in 1949 to literally make a mountain out of a molehill. There's no mountain anywhere in sight.

slide1.text: Juan Pujol García was a Spanish spy who worked as a [[double agent]] loyal to the United Kingdom against Nazi Germany during World War II. Eventually the Germans were funding [[a network of 27 agents, all fictitious]].

slide2.heading: Independent spying
paras: His instructions were to move to Britain and recruit a network of British agents. He moved instead to Lisbon; using a tourist's guide to Britain, he created seemingly credible reports that appeared to come from London.
He made several mistakes, such as claiming that his alleged contact in Glasgow [["would do anything for a litre of wine"]].

slide3.heading: Work with MI6
paras: He reported that his (fabricated) Liverpool agent had fallen ill just before a major fleet movement from that port, and so was unable to report the event. To support this story, [[the agent eventually "died"]] and an obituary was placed in the local newspaper. The Germans were also persuaded to [[pay a pension to the agent's "widow"]].

Juan Pujol García.caption: Juan Pujol García: a Spanish double agent who invented 27 fake spies for the Nazis and fed them fake news about D-Day, then got medals from both sides: an Iron Cross from Germany and an MBE from Britain.

slide1.text: Freddy Got Fingered is a 2001 American surreal black comedy film directed by Tom Green. The film was overwhelmingly panned by critics at the time. Some also referred to it as [[one of the worst films of all time]].

slide2.heading: Critical response
paras: Roger Ebert gave the film a rare zero-star rating and described the film thus: "This movie doesn't scrape the bottom of the barrel. This movie isn't the bottom of the barrel. This movie isn't below the bottom of the barrel. This movie doesn't deserve to be [[mentioned in the same sentence with barrels]]."

slide3.heading: Accolades
paras: The film received eight Golden Raspberry Award nominations in 2002, winning five. Green personally appeared at the ceremony to accept his awards, [[bringing his own red carpet]]. Green would go on to play the harmonica badly for so long that he was [[dragged off the stage]].

Freddy Got Fingered.caption: Freddy Got Fingered: critics called Tom Green's 2001 comedy one of the worst films ever made. When it won five Razzies, Green showed up with his own red carpet and played the harmonica until he was dragged off the stage.

slide1.text: Mattel v. MCA Records was a series of lawsuits between Mattel and MCA Records that resulted from the 1997 hit single [["Barbie Girl" by Danish-Norwegian group Aqua]]. The case was ultimately dismissed.

slide2.heading: Background
paras: Mattel claimed the song violated the Barbie trademark and turned Barbie into a sex object, referring to her as a "Blonde Bimbo." MCA contested Mattel's claims and filed a counterclaim for defamation after [[Mattel had likened MCA to a bank robber]].

slide3.heading: Background
paras: On appeal, the Ninth Circuit ruled the song was protected as a parody, in an opinion penned by Judge Alex Kozinski. Kozinski concluded his ruling by famously saying, [["The parties are advised to chill."]]

Mattel, Inc. v. MCA Records, Inc..caption: Mattel, Inc. v. MCA Records, Inc.: Barbie's maker sued over Aqua's "Barbie Girl" and lost, with the judge telling both sides to "chill." Years later, Mattel's own Barbie movie used a song that samples it.

slide1.text: "Why did the chicken cross the road?" is a riddle joke with the answer being "To get to the other side." It is an example of [[anti-humor]], in that the setup of the joke leads the listener to expect a punchline, but they are instead given a simple statement of fact.

slide2.heading: History
paras: According to music critic Gary Giddins, the joke was spread through the United States by minstrel shows beginning in the 1840s as [[one of the first national jokes]].
In the 1890s, a pun variant appeared: "Why should not a chicken cross the road? [[It would be a fowl proceeding.]]"

slide3.heading: Variations
paras: One class of variations enlists a creature other than the chicken to cross the road. For example, a dinosaur crosses [["because chickens didn't exist yet"]].
"Why did Darth Vader cross the road? To get to the Dark Side."
"Why did the chicken cross the Möbius strip? [[To get to the same side.]]"

Why did the chicken cross the road?.caption: Why did the chicken cross the road?: the classic anti-joke was already in print in 1847, and minstrel shows spread it across America as one of the first national jokes.

slide1.text: There have been multiple prison escapes where an inmate [[escapes by means of a helicopter]]. France has had more recorded helicopter prison escape attempts than any other country, with at least 11.

extraSlides.heading: Michel Vaujour
paras: He made his way to the roof by threatening guards with a fake pistol and [[nectarines painted as grenades]].
On top of the jail he was picked up by his wife Nadine, who had taken helicopter pilot lessons especially for the escape.

extraSlides.heading: Pascal Payet
paras: The [[record for most helicopter escapes]] goes to convicted murderer Pascal Payet.
Payet gained notoriety for using a helicopter in 2001 to escape from Luynes prison and then [[while still on the run]] in 2003 organized another escape for fellow inmates from the same prison.

extraSlides.heading: Mountjoy Jail, Dublin
paras: An IRA member hijacked a helicopter and forced the pilot to land in the exercise yard.
Another prisoner was quoted as saying, "One shamefaced screw said he thought it was the new Minister for Defence arriving. I told him it was [[our Minister of Defence leaving]]."

extraSlides.heading: Vassilis Palaiokostas
paras: Another multiple helicopter escapee is Vassilis Palaiokostas, who escaped for the second time from the same prison.
Their new prison break took place while [[their trial for the 2006 helicopter-assisted escape]] was ongoing. Paleokostas remains at large.

extraSlides.heading: Ben Kramer
paras: Kramer, a famous Apache Boat owner and racer tried to escape by helicopter from the prison. The escape failed when the rookie pilot hovered 12 inches off the ground in a very tight space.
One of the skids caught on the razor wire, causing the helicopter to [[catapult over the fence and crash into the prison grounds]].

extraSlides.heading: Lucy Dudko and John Killick
paras: Librarian Lucy Dudko hired a helicopter under the pretence of [[checking out the upcoming Olympic site]] in Sydney. Waiting was Killick, who was serving 28 years for armed robbery.
Killick was released, but is not allowed to have contact with Dudko [[until he turns 80 years old]].

List of helicopter prison escapes.caption: List of helicopter prison escapes: France leads the world in helicopter jailbreaks. In one, a man threatened guards with nectarines painted as grenades, then got plucked off the prison roof by his wife, who had taken flying lessons just for the escape.

slide1.text: The Beginning Was the End is a 1971 pseudo-scientific book which claims [[humankind evolved from cannibalistic apes]]. The book's legacy comes largely from the new wave band [[Devo]].

slide2.heading: Synopsis
paras: The Beginning Was the End claimed that modern humans devolved from a species of brain-eating apes. Maerth offered no evidence for his theories, basing them largely on his alleged meetings with cannibals and his experiences [[eating raw ape brains in a restaurant]] in Southeast Asia.
He hints at having activated his latent psychic abilities through [[altering the shape of his skull]].

slide3.heading: Popular culture
paras: Devo incorporated several elements of the book into their concept of "de-evolution" and even adopted the book's title for their short film.
Gerald V. Casale said of the book, [["It's a better story than the Bible as far as DEVO's concerned."]]

The Beginning Was the End.caption: The Beginning Was the End: a 1971 book claimed humans evolved from brain-eating apes, based largely on the author eating raw ape brains in a restaurant. The band Devo built their whole "de-evolution" idea around it.

slide1.text: I Love You, Colonel Sanders! is a dating sim commissioned by the restaurant chain KFC. The primary objective of the player is to develop a romantic relationship with [[KFC's founder Colonel Sanders]], portrayed as [[an attractive classmate at a cooking school]].

slide2.heading: Gameplay
paras: The game takes place over a three-day semester at the fictional [[University of Cooking School: Academy for Learning]], where the player character is studying to become a chef.
The player is presented with dialog choices that present opportunities to [[win Sanders' favor]], as well as interactions with rivals Aeshleigh and [[Van Van the Man Man]].

slide3.heading: Reception
paras: In her review for Kotaku, Gita Jackson criticized the game's over-reliance on "zaniness".
Nicole Carpenter of Polygon criticized it as [["less of a game and more of a marketing stunt"]].
Metacritic gave the game an aggregate score of 50/100.

I Love You, Colonel Sanders!.caption: I Love You, Colonel Sanders!: KFC really made a free dating game where you try to win over a dreamy classmate version of Colonel Sanders at cooking school.

slide1.text: The "Dancing Baby", also called "the Oogachacka Baby", is an Internet meme of a 3D-rendered animation of [[a baby performing a cha-cha type dance]]. It quickly became one of the first viral videos in 1996.

slide2.heading: Origin
paras: The 3-D model of the baby was based on [[a scan of a plastic doll]].
Unreal Pictures co-founder Michael Girard had discarded the Dancing Baby, opining it was [["disturbing" for its realistic nature]].

slide3.heading: Spread
paras: A popular variation contained the song [["Hooked on a Feeling"]] by Blue Swede, hence the name "Oogachacka Baby".
Woodell's animated GIF later proceeded to show up in mainstream media, including television dramas such as [[Ally McBeal]].

Dancing baby.caption: Dancing baby: a 3D baby doing the cha-cha became one of the internet's first viral videos in 1996. Its 3D model came from a scan of a plastic doll, and one of its creators had thrown it out for being "disturbing."

slide1.text: Raël is a French journalist and religious leader who founded and leads the Raëlian Movement, an international [[UFO religion]]. Before becoming a religious leader, Raël, then known as Claude Vorilhon, worked as a sports car journalist and test driver.

slide2.heading: The Raëlian messages
paras: On December 3, 1973 in a secluded area within a French volcanic crater, Vorilhon claimed to see "something like a bell" made of shiny metal coming out from the sky. According to Vorilhon, the face of the extraterrestrial was [["full of love."]]
He claimed that he was contacted by one of the Elohim, who took him to another planet to [[meet Buddha, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad]].

slide3.heading: Promoted technologies
paras: Raël believes that humans are slowly transitioning into a society wherein they will not need to work or have jobs. This is because humans [["are not made to work"]].
He said that he was presented [[genetically modified flowers, that swayed and changed colors with music]], while on another planet.

Raël.caption: Raël: a former French race-car journalist who says aliens took him to another planet to meet Buddha, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad, and who then founded a UFO religion.

slide1.text: Minions is a village in Cornwall, England. Minions is first recorded in 1613 and its meaning is unknown. The village has embraced the coincidence that its name is now shared with [[the Despicable Me characters]].

slide2.heading: Popular culture
paras: In May 2015, a custom welcome sign for the village of Minions featured images of Minions. The sign caused traffic and safety issues from vehicles stopping to take photos.
After several months it was replaced with an ordinary, [[Minions-free sign]], but an anonymous person then decorated the plain "Welcome to Minions" sign with [[two stickers of Minions]].

slide3.heading: Tony & The Bull
paras: A previous resident of Minions and his rather unusual bovine friend were featured in an award-winning short film "Tony & The Bull".

Scrunch, a Highland bull, was found as a calf on the moor, and [[Tony house-trained him]] and lived in a former run-down pub close to Minions. Both have since died and were [[cremated and buried together]].

Minions, Cornwall.caption: Minions, Cornwall: a real English village that shares its name with the Despicable Me characters. When it put Minions on its welcome sign, so many drivers stopped for photos that it caused traffic problems.

slide1.text: Wise Men of Gotham is the name given to the people of Gotham, Nottinghamshire, in allusion to an incident where they supposedly [[feigned idiocy to avoid a Royal visit]]. The most notable use of the name Gotham was by Bill Finger in naming the home of [[Batman]].

slide2.heading: Legend
paras: King John's messengers found some of the inhabitants engaged in endeavouring to [[drown an eel in a pool of water]]; others were tumbling their cheeses down a hill, [[that they might find their way to Nottingham]] for sale; and some were employed in hedging in a cuckoo.

slide3.heading: Legacy
paras: Reminded of the foolish ingenuity of Gotham's residents, Washington Irving gave the name "Gotham" to [[New York City]].

In a story titled "Cityscape" in Batman Chronicles, Robin reads a journal that tells of how Gotham got its name: "We could call it 'Gotham' after a village in England – where, according to common belief, [[all are bereft of their wits]]."

Wise Men of Gotham.caption: Wise Men of Gotham: the villagers of Gotham, England, supposedly acted like fools to keep King John away, trying to drown an eel and rolling cheeses to market. Their village later lent its name to New York City and to Batman's Gotham City.
